title: Bound on walks contained in a set
statement: Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space of size $n$, and let $\[?]$ denote its operator norm on vectors orthogonal to the uniform vector. Suppose this quantity is at most $\lambda$, with $0\leq\lambda\leq1$. If $B$ is a set of states and $0\leq\beta$ satisfies $|B|\leq\beta n$, then for every $k\in\mathbb N$, the probability that all states of a length-$k$ walk lie in $B$ is at most $\bigl((1-\lambda)\sqrt{\beta}+\lambda\bigr)^k$.
hypotheses_covered: Each row of A sums to one
The spectral quantity lambda(A) is at most lambda
B is a subset of the state space
caveat: The definition of lambda uses a supremum over unit vectors orthogonal to the uniform vector; for a one-state space this set is empty, so its value may not match the usual operator norm description.
